checks.title: Callers and consumers still get the contract they rely on
evidence_required: the contract (signature, format, schema, documented behavior)
each affected caller or consumer and what it relies on
falsifiers: no caller depends on the changed behavior
the change is additive and old inputs behave identically
validation_methods: run an approved test against base and head
checks.limits: Unknown external consumers stay unknown (cite the recon gap); never assume none.

checks.title: Errors reach a handler that can act, with their cause
evidence_required: where the error is raised or returned
every path it takes to a handler
falsifiers: a caller handles or re-raises it
the error is impossible given validated input
validation_methods: an approved command that triggers the error
checks.limits: A swallowed error is a candidate only when an observable consequence follows.

checks.title: Resources and state are released or rolled back on every path
evidence_required: release on success, error and cancellation paths
falsifiers: a context manager, finally or owner releases it
process exit is the intended release
validation_methods: an approved test that injects a failure
checks.limits: Startup, migration and shutdown paths are in scope; difficult to test is not untestable.

checks.title: Shared state is safe under the concurrency the code actually has
evidence_required: the concurrent entry points that touch it
falsifiers: a lock, transaction or queue serializes it
validation_methods: an approved stress or race test
checks.limits: Name the concurrency source (threads, async tasks, workers, retries); do not assume it.

checks.title: Inputs cannot drive unbounded memory, time, retries or output
evidence_required: the loop, allocation or retry it drives
falsifiers: input size is fixed by a trusted producer
validation_methods: trace the size from source to use
an approved run with a large input
checks.limits: Report the bound that is missing, not a performance opinion.

checks.title: Untrusted input is validated once at the trust boundary
evidence_required: the validation (or its absence) before first use
falsifiers: validation happens earlier on every path
the producer is trusted and versioned
validation_methods: trace from boundary to first use
an approved test with invalid input
checks.limits: Internal callers are trusted; re-validation inside is not required.

checks.title: The code does what its contract and callers expect for the stated inputs
evidence_required: the expected behavior (contract, docstring, test, spec or report)
the code path for the triggering input
falsifiers: callers never pass the triggering input
the documented behavior is what the code does
validation_methods: evaluate the path by hand for a concrete input
an approved test with that input
checks.limits: Expected behavior must come from a source, not preference.
